extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, exporters, industry groups, NGOs, and other stakeholders preparing public comments on ITAR/EAR arms export control proposed rules
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on arms export proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting effective public comments on State Department / ATF proposed rulemakings affecting ITAR/EAR export controls, including procedural submission instructions and substantive topics/criteria to address (national security, costs, multilateral regimes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can be submitted via: - Federal e-rulemaking portal: regulations.gov (will not accept comments after midnight Eastern Time on the last day) - Mail: ATF Rulemaking Comments; Mail Stop 6N-518, Office of Regulatory Affairs; Enforcement Programs and Services; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; 99 New York Ave, NE; Washington, DC 20226
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the specific RIN in the subject (e.g., RIN 1140-AA77). Note the portal deadline (midnight ET on the last day) and include full mail address exactly for mailed submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific USML categories or CCL ECCNs being amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific USML categories or CCL ECCNs being amended
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the exact USML category or Commerce Control List ECCN entries affected so reviewers can see the scope and technical reach of the proposed change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Arms Export Control Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Arms Export Control Act (22 USC § 2778) provisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the statute and relevant provisions when discussing legal authority, policy alignment, or statutory constraints for the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address national security implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule would affect U.S. national security, including risks of diversion, impact on military capabilities, or security partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include manufacturer/exporter compliance cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative cost estimates (preferably supported by data) for compliance burdens on manufacturers and exporters, including implementation and ongoing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impacts on foreign policy objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impacts on foreign policy objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the proposed rule would support or undermine U.S. foreign policy goals, alliances, and diplomatic initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference multilateral export control regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Wassenaar Arrangement, MTCR, and other multilateral regimes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, compare the proposal to commitments or practices under multilateral regimes (Wassenaar, MTCR, etc.) and explain consistency or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide industry impact data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide industry impact data (jobs, exports, R&D)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply empirical data on employment, export volumes, and R&D effects to substantiate claims about industry impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address congressional notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether the proposed rule triggers statutory or procedural congressional notification/consultation obligations and discuss compliance or timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify dual-use considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss items with both civilian and military applications and how controls should balance legitimate trade with security concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider non-proliferation impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the proposal affects non-proliferation objectives, including risks to chemical, biological, nuclear, or missile-related proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer between USML and CCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of items between USML and CCL
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss criteria and consequences of moving items from the United States Munitions List to the Commerce Control List or vice versa, including licensing and policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of defense articles/components/parts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on proposed definitional changes or clarifications and their practical effects on classification, licensing, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brokering controls
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address scope of brokering controls, who is covered, and how proposed rules would affect intermediary transactions and broker reporting/authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-export and retransfer controls
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss controls on downstream transfers, potential end-use/end-user restrictions, and mechanisms to prevent unauthorized retransfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: License application procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feedback on proposed licensing processes, timing, evidentiary requirements, and any burdens or ambiguities that could hinder lawful trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-specific embargoes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on proposed country-specific restrictions or sanctions-related controls and their alignment with U.S. policy and international obligations.
